name: Control-Point Selection for Point Cloud Annotation
summary: In a VR point cloud, the user points at one point with the controller or with the eyes and presses a button; nearby points with similar local features are labelled automatically, so a few control points annotate a whole object.
howItWorks: Built for a Meta Quest Pro. In one mode the ray comes from the hand controller, in the other from eye tracking; in both, a button on the controller confirms. The point picked is the one inside a narrow cone-shaped volume around the ray (limited near the origin) that best matches the ray, with filtering over several frames to reduce ray noise in dense clouds. A shortest-path-tree algorithm then spreads the label from each control point to neighbouring points using local features. Compared with bounding-box selection for VR annotation, both modes improved annotation quality and reduced annotation time.
advantages: Annotates irregular shapes with a few clicks instead of drawing boxes.
Works with gaze or hand pointing.
limitations: Designed for point cloud labelling; accuracy depends on the automatic segmentation around each control point.

relationships.note: Uses a gaze ray as one of its two pointing modes.
Uses a controller ray as one of its two pointing modes.
